answer: Each identity must finish a prescribed chain of dependent modular squarings before producing a Wesolowski proof; each square depends on the previous result. An attacker may run separate clone chains on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize the work within a chain to make that identity finish sooner. Sybil resistance therefore comes from multiplying hardware, energy, and elapsed-time costs per clone—not from making parallel clones impossible. Like an atlas, vine, or ember, these are distinct instances, not shortcuts through the same computation.
